decisions.reason: SOL keeps the metallic clatter without changing the image.
“Heart seize” is awkward English; “seize up” preserves the source’s physical reaction naturally.
SOL preserves the reason for his presence and folds the distance-based risk into this paragraph.
The distance-based risk is retained in H003, so deleting this duplicate is faithful.
“First” adds no meaning; SOL keeps the concealment-technique regret.
The source emphatically says the regret came far too late; BASE preserves that emphasis.
SOL keeps the causal sequence and the brawl-as-curriculum joke.
“Hipster sect with a pedigree” naturally preserves the source’s established-roots joke.
“Its” clearly refers to the Fire Gate Clan already named in context.
“Treating” keeps the insult’s meaning and the narrator’s irreverent voice.
The mob and rainbow-colored clubs preserve the joke; “lineage had carried on” keeps the continuity.
SOL keeps the ancestors’ policies as the cause of his predicament.
“My mouth went dry” naturally preserves the source’s dry-lips reaction.
SOL preserves his approach and questioning of guards who abandoned their post.
The shorter phrasing keeps the guards’ excuse and hesitation.
“Traitors” naturally conveys people harboring treasonous intentions in this context.
“We’re truly sorry” preserves the guards’ apology and trailing qualification.
The present-tense taunt keeps the same implication that they may not want to serve.
The article-free question keeps the drill-sergeant joke in natural speech.
The split sentences preserve the narrator’s suspicion and the sudden remark.
“Your superior” works distributively for each guard, and “turn in” preserves the order to return their gear.
The concise idiom preserves the shock.
“Waiting desperately” preserves the narrator’s anxious hope that Hogun would leave.
The source says this is an order he gives in his capacity as Thousand Captain; SOL drops his personal authority from the phrasing.
The source says to hit him once; the one-time action remains implicit in “Just punch him.”
The source says he cheered them earnestly; SOL’s “silently” changes that attitude.
The source’s blunt “do as you’re told” military maxim is better preserved by BASE’s idiom than SOL’s generalized description.
Naming Jeong Hogun makes the referent explicit without changing who they would defy.
The men’s target is clear from context; omitting the repeated name preserves the meaning.
The weak replies, lowered rain hats, and trudging departure are all retained.
The short reversal keeps the same interrupted-action beat.
SOL preserves the unexpected arrival while naturally referring back to Hogun’s appearance.
The streamlined wording preserves the challenge about dismissing Imperial Guards on a whim.
The robe, puddle, rain, and Hogun’s pause before speaking remain intact.
The dialogue immediately continues, so omitting “before continuing” loses no action or timing.
“My question” refers clearly to the question just asked and preserves the request for an answer.
The source describes the voice as having long hovered between masculine and feminine; SOL drops that sustained impression.
SOL preserves the hierarchy and the superior’s authority over final punishment in natural dialogue.
“Stared” preserves Hogun’s silent, fixed attention.
“Walk together” naturally conveys Ma’s invitation to accompany him.
“Walk together?” echoes Ma’s invitation naturally and does not change the response.
The important discussion and return to the Inner Palace remain; “I’d like to discuss” is natural speech.
Removing “had” does not change the narrator’s conjecture about Hogun’s intended reply.
Ma Sanbao is the clear referent, and “reluctance” preserves Hogun’s aversion in context.
The half-beat timing is preserved without the redundant transition.
SOL retains the curtailed East Depot, the Guard’s rise, and Ma’s leadership in Cang Gong’s place.
The initiative, easy smile, and shoulder pat are preserved.
“Plenty I need to hear” naturally preserves Ma’s intention to hear from the Guard.
“A martial artist through and through” preserves Hogun’s characterization and Ma’s advantage.
SOL correctly has Hogun leave with Ma and incorporates the warning that BASE splits into H051.
The warning is retained in H050, so deleting this repeated sentence is faithful.
The guards’ salute, Hogun turning away, the narrator’s relief, and the Sound Transmission remain.
The message is delivered by Sound Transmission, not the narrator’s thought; BASE’s em-dash format preserves that distinction better than SOL’s italics.
“Looking my way” and the wink preserve the gesture and its target.
The slight surprise and subsequent recognition are unchanged.
“Spotting my amateurish attempt” preserves the meaning without changing established terminology.
“I had no idea” naturally conveys the narrator’s uncertainty.
“Brought the assassins … into this” preserves his uncertainty about how they became involved.
“Still nearby” and “detect me” preserve the guards’ inability to sense his presence.
“Swish” is a natural rendering of the brief movement sound.
The darkness, rain, and thunder are retained together in the image of his movement.
The weather’s assistance is retained in H061, so deleting this fragment avoids repetition.
The source specifically says he leapt over the pavilions and walls; “clearing” changes the physical action.
“Have you seen” naturally asks whether the guards have seen him.
The shorter reply preserves the comparison to a monster.
The emphatic appetite, pork, plate count, and cooks’ reaction remain intact.
“I’d heard about him” naturally preserves that the speaker had heard of the story.
The Korean frames the prediction as something people say; SOL states it as certain.
The suggestion to kick him out and the speaker’s impressed reaction remain.
The source says they cannot treat the guests poorly over pork; SOL changes that to not turning them away.
“Said his name” naturally preserves the point that they only called him “that guy.”
Looking heavenward and sighing remain, followed by noticing the group.
“A dozen or so” naturally conveys the approximate group size.
The strong, sinus-clearing smell is preserved in natural phrasing.
SOL keeps the Outer Palace lodging and the narrator’s surprise at finding them this way.
The Hansel and Gretel comparison and silent following are preserved.
“Fired off curses in a steady stream” keeps the cook’s rapid string of curses.
The crude plea and trailing interruption preserve the cook’s anger without softening it.
The brief transition preserves the moment he sees the knife.
The trembling knife remains clear and its holder is identified by context.
The Korean says the door opened roughly; SOL omits that physical detail.
SOL preserves the cook’s lack of martial training and genuine killing intent.
The familiar face peeking from the darkness behind the food-bearing group is retained.
The added exclamation mark preserves the startled interruption.
“Take some of this food” naturally preserves the cook’s request and complaint.
The attendants and plates are retained in H087, so this deletion does not drop the action.
SOL retains the sharp reply, palace attendants setting down plates, and the poisoning warning.
The breeze reopening the door just after the group leaves remains intact.
The aside preserves how the event appeared to outside observers.
The Fire King is already identified as Jeok Cheongang in context, so omitting the repeated name is faithful.
